exit: RESOLVED 2026-07-28: --bootstrap-expect N. Every seed advertises N in the serf tag bootstrap_expect; core/consensus.PlanBootstrap is a pure function of the gossip view that reports not-ready until N matching seeds are visible, then names the lowest node id as the single bootstrapper and returns the full initial configuration. The one-shot serf Join now retries while the set is incomplete - seed nodes legitimately start in any order. What it does establish is one authorization codepath per mutation, a subject binding, and an auditable revocable token id; caller-supplied tokens plug into the same seam without moving a call site. Artifacts: 3 rights unit tests, 5 refusal subtests proving the gate runs BEFORE the action (a nil scheduler would panic otherwise), and a scoping test asserting exactly one right and the named subject.

exit: RESOLVED 2026-07-28: CI now runs 'mage vuln' between the build and the test suite, so a reachable CVE fails the build instead of accruing as an alert. Triage on 2026-07-28 found none of the alerts call-reachable: every x/crypto CVE lives in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh or ssh/agent, and the build graph imports only chacha20poly1305, curve25519, hkdf, pbkdf2 and scrypt; CVE-2026-25680 is in x/net/html against a graph that imports x/net/ipv4, ipv6 and bpf; CVE-2026-40898 is HTTP/3 QPACK trailer expansion in quic-go/http3, and the control plane speaks raw QUIC streams demuxed by ALPN, never http3. The alerts were still wrong to be sitting open: version-range scanners cannot see reachability, so an unpatched floor is indistinguishable from an exploitable one to anyone reading the repo from outside. Bumped to clear the floors: golang.org/x/crypto 0.50.0 -> 0.53.0 (0.52.0 is the advisory floor; 0.53.0 is what x/net 0.56.0 demands), golang.org/x/net 0.53.0 -> 0.56.0, golang.org/x/text 0.36.0 -> 0.39.0, github.com/klauspost/compress 1.17.9 -> 1.18.7, and github.com/quic-go/quic-go 0.57.1 -> 0.59.1. The quic-go jump crosses two minor versions on the module the shared listener is built on and needed no source change. Remaining and permanent: GO-2026-5932 (golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp is unmaintained) has no fixed version, so it stays a module-level finding for as long as anything in the graph requires x/crypto. It is not imported, and govulncheck's call-graph filter is what keeps it from failing the gate - which is the reason the gate is govulncheck and not a version-range scanner. Artifacts: govulncheck reports 0 called and 0 imported vulnerabilities (was 1 imported, 23 in required modules); lint 0 issues / 0 nosec; 'go test -race ./...' green across all 10 packages; the tagged cluster e2e green in 39.3s, which is the load-bearing one - raft, serf and the RPC plane all ride the quic-go listener that moved two minor versions.
